title: The month potato prices jumped across India
summary: In July 2024, the median potato market moved +17.2% in a month, 2.6 standard deviations from the usual for that month.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the 2.6σ seasonal move is among the largest on record for potato, across 763 reporting markets.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of daily modal prices; markets need ≥5 reports in both months
caveats: Many market points are district centres, not mandi gates.
Modal prices are reported aggregates, not transaction offers.

scenes.headline: July 2024
scenes.caption: Potato prices across 763 markets that reported in both June 2024 and July 2024.

scenes.headline: Median move +17.2%
scenes.caption: The typical market's potato price jumped 17.2% in one month. 88% of markets moved the same way.

scenes.headline: 2.6× the usual swing
scenes.caption: Compared with the same month in every earlier year on record, this move was 2.6 standard deviations from normal.

scenes.headline: Tamil Nadu
scenes.caption: Neighbouring markets moved together: the 78 reporting markets in Tamil Nadu had a median change of +9900.0%.

scenes.headline: Murliganj
scenes.caption: Murliganj (Bihar), one of the busiest markets among the biggest movers: monthly median ₹2,000 → ₹3,000 per quintal (+50.0%).

scenes.headline: What this does and doesn't show
scenes.caption: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

conclusion: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

title: The potato storage gamble
summary: Agra potatoes: ₹1,290 in March 2024, ₹2,010 in October. Break-even storage budget: ₹489 per quintal.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the yearly harvest-to-autumn storage question at Agra, with 10 earlier seasons to learn from.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of Agra daily modal prices (≥8 reports)
caveats: No cold-storage rent is cited, so no net profit is claimed.
Stored and fresh potatoes may differ in grade.

scenes.headline: March 2024
scenes.caption: Potatoes are harvested in early spring and often held in cold stores in western Uttar Pradesh, which the RBI paper calls the potato belt's key selling point.

scenes.headline: Harvest price
scenes.caption: Agra's March 2024 median: ₹1,290 per quintal.

scenes.headline: The informed bet
scenes.caption: Using only the 10 earlier years, March→October had averaged +₹400. A rule-following trader would store.

scenes.headline: October 2024
scenes.caption: October median: ₹2,010, a change of +55.8%.

scenes.headline: Shrinkage and interest
scenes.caption: Allowing 7% loss and 12% a year interest for 7 months leaves a storage budget of ₹489 per quintal.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: Seven months of storage needed to cost less than ₹489 per quintal to break even. Cold-storage rents are not in our cited evidence, so AGRINET does not claim a profit.

assumptions.value: not in cited evidence; shown as break-even budget

conclusion: Seven months of storage needed to cost less than ₹489 per quintal to break even. Cold-storage rents are not in our cited evidence, so AGRINET does not claim a profit.

sources.title: Agmarknet / data.gov.in daily mandi modal prices (retained AGRINET snapshot)
RBI Working Paper WPS (DEPR) 08/2024 — Price Dynamics of Tomato, Onion and Potato

title: A thin potato margin that breaks under stress
summary: Agra → Vashi New Mumbai, November 2024: a ₹700 per quintal median price gap on 29 matched days. After modeled costs: ₹186 per quintal on the typical day.
why_selected: Chosen automatically for November 2024: one of AGRINET's documented trade corridors with 29 matched report days.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices; sale matched to the first destination report 1–3 days after transit
caveats: Hypothetical: no actual shipment is claimed.
Modal prices may mix varieties and grades (mostly FAQ).
Costs are survey values and assumptions, not quotes.
OSRM car profile; truck route not verified.

scenes.headline: November 2024
scenes.caption: Agra sits in western Uttar Pradesh's cold-stored potato belt; Vashi supplies Mumbai.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: On 29 matched days, Agra reported a median ₹1,930 per quintal; Vashi New Mumbai reported ₹2,600 2 days later.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹700/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gross gap was ₹700 per quintal and was positive on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 1,270 km by road
scenes.caption: Routed road distance 1,270 km (OpenStreetMap car routing, ~15 driving hours). Trucks are slower; we allow 2 days.

scenes.headline: Now add the costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹273/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. Modeled net on the typical (median) day: ₹186 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Stress test
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day becomes −₹14 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Hindsight vs. a real trader
scenes.caption: With perfect hindsight, 26 of 29 days cleared modeled costs. A trader using only reports available on the day would have shipped on 26 of 29 days, averaging ₹157 per quintal; 3 of those shipments lost money.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: A modeled surplus survived baseline costs but not the stress test, so it depended on everything going right. A trader acting on the previous report did average ₹157 per quintal under baseline costs, but −₹43 under the stress test.

assumptions.value: scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹273/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days

conclusion: A modeled surplus survived baseline costs but not the stress test, so it depended on everything going right. A trader acting on the previous report did average ₹157 per quintal under baseline costs, but −₹43 under the stress test.

title: The potato trade that looked profitable but wasn't
summary: Agra → Vashi New Mumbai, December 2024: a ₹190 per quintal median price gap on 31 matched days. After modeled costs: −₹264 per quintal on the typical day.
why_selected: Chosen automatically for December 2024: one of AGRINET's documented trade corridors with 31 matched report days.

scenes.headline: December 2024
scenes.caption: Agra sits in western Uttar Pradesh's cold-stored potato belt; Vashi supplies Mumbai.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: On 31 matched days, Agra reported a median ₹1,780 per quintal; Vashi New Mumbai reported ₹1,850 2 days later.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹190/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gross gap was ₹190 per quintal and was positive on 84% of days.
